name: Marcus "Tiny" Bell
equipment: Aluminum baseball bat (from behind the bar)
Remington 870 pump shotgun (6 shells), the bar's 'last resort' — he has fired it twice in his life
Bar towel, bottle opener, a roll of duct tape
features: Specialist (Human (Specialist): +2 Strength, +1 Constitution, extra skill proficiency in Insight)
Hard Hitter (unarmed strikes deal 1d6 + STR bludgeoning, and may use DEX; after taking the Attack action he can make an unarmed strike as a bonus action)
Hard to Kill (when reduced to 0 HP but not killed outright, he drops to 1 HP instead; once per long rest)
Proficiencies (Melee, Sidearms, Longarms; Light and Medium armor)
Local Hero (Athlete feature: everyone in Corbin's Ferry over the age of thirty remembers the 2009 state semifinal, and most of them will give him a hearing, a meal or a hand)

personality.traits: I am the biggest person in most rooms and I make myself small in them: I sit down, I speak quietly, I let people come to me. Then, when it matters, I stand up.
personality.ideals: You protect the people in your house. That was the whole job at the door of the Landing Bar for twelve years, and it is still the whole job.
personality.bonds: My regulars. The Landing Bar is a dive, and they are drunks and farmers and old men, and they are mine.
personality.flaws: I go in first, every time, without looking. My knees are shot and I will not admit it until they give out.

appearance: Thirty-five, six foot five and about three hundred pounds, Black, with a shaved head, a short greying beard and a gap-toothed grin. Wears a battered black-and-gold letterman's jacket, a Landing Bar T-shirt and work boots, and moves with the slightly careful gait of a man with two bad knees.
backstory: Marcus Bell was the best offensive lineman Haskett County High ever had, played two years at Mizzou before his knees went, came home, and has run the door — and lately the whole place — at the Landing Bar on Front Street ever since. Everyone calls him Tiny and has since he was twelve. He knows every drunk in town by first name, has broken up a thousand fights and started none, and on Saturday afternoon of Ferry Days he was hauling kegs to the beer garden when the screaming started. He got three people into the walk-in cooler and held the door with his back while something on the other side of it beat on it for ten minutes. He would like very much never to have to do that again, and he knows he will.
